# Articulation link

Query target: `ARTICULATION_LINK`. These are static capabilities; the live session decides which objects and operations are available. See [session semantics](../data_model.md) and [write behavior](../writable.md).

Shapes describe tensor dimensions; lanes describe the tuple width, not an extra dimension. Ordering is row-major unless stated otherwise. **CPU** means host memory; **scene device** means CPU on CPU/readback scenes or CUDA on DirectGPU; **CUDA** requires CUDA. Symbolic sizes come from the live group.

## isSleeping

`u8`; units: [dimensionless](units.md#dimensionless).

| Access | Layout | Memory |
|---|---|---|
| Read | fixed, shape [objects], 1 lanes | CPU |

Current PhysX sleep state, independent of the last wake command. A link reports its owning articulation. DirectGPU disables sleeping, so emitted values are zero; omitted rows are not awake values.

## worldScale

`f32`; units: [dimensionless](units.md#dimensionless); frame: world.

| Access | Layout | Memory |
|---|---|---|
| Read | fixed, shape [objects], 3 lanes | scene device |

**Read:** requires [DirectGPU warmup](#directgpu-warmup).

The scale physics built the link's collision shapes with: the parser's signed decomposition of the link's world transform when the link was created (a replicated clone copies its source's). PhysX carries no scale. Composes with position and orientation (same physics frame) into the link's world matrix. Constant for the link's lifetime: articulation links do not apply a runtime scale edit, so they keep simulating, and reporting, the creation scale. DirectGPU serves it from a stored device copy, beside the pose. No point-instancer array form.

## Conditions

### DirectGPU warmup

Device-backed DirectGPU state requires a completed first step; a write never warms the simulation automatically.

### Kinematic target

Writing requires standalone kinematic bodies on CPU/readback; DirectGPU and articulation-link writes are refused. Reads fall back to current pose without a target.

### Native pointer

Borrowed native address, valid only while the object remains alive. Does not confer ownership or bypass runtime synchronization. Structural changes (adding, removing or re-inserting objects, moving them between scenes, attaching or detaching shapes) through a native PhysX pointer are not recommended: after one, ovphysx reads and writes are not guaranteed to work until the stage is re-attached.
